## 14.4 Host network migration — preallocated-static cutover

::: {.callout-warning}
**Before you start:** make sure you have **console access via iDRAC** available. If you lose
IP connectivity over SSH after a netplan change, the iDRAC Virtual Console (§3.6) is your
recovery path. The §14.5 iDRAC migration runs **in parallel** with this one, so by the time
the server lands on the NDMO rack you have both a working iDRAC (on its new NDMO static IP)
and a working host (on its new NDMO static IP) coming up in one boot.
:::

### Overview

Because VBoS and NDMO are on the same GoV WAN (§14 intro), the host network change is a
**subnet reassignment within the same logical network**, not a cross-network migration. The
clean path is therefore:

| Step | Where it runs | What happens |
|:-:|---|---|
| **A** | **At VBoS, before the move** | Disable cloud-init network, author the final NDMO static block as a netplan drop-in (`99-ndmo-static.yaml`) with `dhcp4: false`; leave the current `50-cloud-init.yaml` untouched so reboots on the VBoS rack still come up on `10.4.26.55`. |
| **B** | **At VBoS, before the move** | Realign host DNS to the GoV resolvers (`10.255.134.24 / 10.255.134.5`). This is a standalone fix that does not depend on the IP migration and should happen regardless. |
| **C** | **At NDMO, at power-up** | Remove (or truncate) `50-cloud-init.yaml`; `99-ndmo-static.yaml` becomes authoritative; one `netplan generate && netplan apply` brings the host up on the NDMO IP in one step. |
| **D** | **At NDMO, after cutover** | Verify + `hostnamectl` + update application config (§14.6). |

A **DHCP-detour fallback** is documented in §14.4.x for the case where NDMO networking can't
pre-issue the static IP in time for Step A.

### Step A — Pre-allocate the NDMO static IP (at VBoS, before the move)

Values to have in hand from NDMO networking **before** this step:

- `<NDMO-STATIC-IP>` and `<CIDR>` (e.g. `10.5.12.40/24`)
- `<NDMO-GATEWAY>` (e.g. `10.5.12.1`)
- `<NDMO-FQDN>` (e.g. `ndmo-drmis-01.ndmo.gov.vu` — must match the `A` record NDMO will publish in `vangov.local` DNS)

The server uses **netplan** (Ubuntu 24.04 default). Current active file is
**cloud-init-managed**:

```
/etc/netplan/50-cloud-init.yaml
```

Live contents (verified on 2026-04-23):

```yaml
network:
  version: 2
  ethernets:
    eno8303:
      dhcp4: no
      addresses:
        - 10.4.26.55/24
      routes:
        - to: default
          via: 10.4.26.1
      nameservers:
        addresses:
          - 8.8.8.8
          - 1.1.1.1
```

**Because cloud-init re-writes this file at every boot**, edits to it do not survive. Disable
cloud-init's network module once (this is a pending item in §13):

```bash
echo 'network: {config: disabled}' | \
  sudo tee /etc/cloud/cloud.cfg.d/99-disable-network-config.cfg
```

Keep `50-cloud-init.yaml` as-is for now (so the box stays reachable on `10.4.26.55`), and
author the NDMO static config as a **higher-priority drop-in**. Netplan merges all
`/etc/netplan/*.yaml` files, and the higher-numbered filename wins on conflicts — so
`99-ndmo-static.yaml` will override `50-cloud-init.yaml` as soon as it is in place.

**Author the drop-in but do not apply it yet** (we don't want the IP to change while the box
is still in the VBoS rack):

```bash
sudo tee /etc/netplan/99-ndmo-static.yaml.disabled >/dev/null <<'YAML'
# Final NDMO static config — applied at cutover (Step C).
# Cloud-init network management is disabled via
# /etc/cloud/cloud.cfg.d/99-disable-network-config.cfg.
network:
  version: 2
  ethernets:
    eno8303:
      dhcp4: false
      addresses:
        - <NDMO-STATIC-IP>/<CIDR>
      routes:
        - to: default
          via: <NDMO-GATEWAY>
      nameservers:
        addresses:
          - 10.255.134.24    # GoV primary — matches iDRAC
          - 10.255.134.5     # GoV secondary
        search:
          - vangov.local
YAML

sudo chmod 600 /etc/netplan/99-ndmo-static.yaml.disabled
```

The `.disabled` suffix means netplan ignores the file (it only reads `*.yaml`). At cutover
we rename it to `99-ndmo-static.yaml` and reapply.

Back up the current netplan state so Step C has a clean reference:

```bash
sudo cp /etc/netplan/50-cloud-init.yaml \
        /root/50-cloud-init.yaml.pre-handover-$(date +%F)
```

### Step B — Realign host DNS to GoV resolvers (at VBoS, before the move)

**This is independent of the IP move and should happen regardless** — it fixes the
"8.8.8.8 / 1.1.1.1 on a GoV private host" misconfiguration flagged in §6.1 and §13.

```bash
sudo tee /etc/netplan/98-gov-dns.yaml >/dev/null <<'YAML'
# Host DNS realignment to Vanuatu Government resolvers.
# This matches the iDRAC on the same box (domain vangov.local).
network:
  version: 2
  ethernets:
    eno8303:
      nameservers:
        addresses:
          - 10.255.134.24
          - 10.255.134.5
        search:
          - vangov.local
YAML

sudo chmod 600 /etc/netplan/98-gov-dns.yaml
sudo netplan generate
sudo netplan try       # auto-reverts after 120 s unless you confirm
# If SSH stays alive and `resolvectl status` shows the GoV resolvers, press ENTER.
```

Verify:

```bash
resolvectl status eno8303 | grep -E 'DNS Servers|DNS Domain'
# Expected:  DNS Servers: 10.255.134.24 10.255.134.5
#            DNS Domain:  vangov.local

# GoV DNS should now resolve vangov.local names that public DNS could not:
dig +short <some-gov-hostname>.vangov.local
```

```{=html}
<div class="screenshot-slot"><div class="screenshot-slot-inner"><strong>Figure 14.4.1 — Host DNS realigned to GoV resolvers</strong><code>docs/screenshots/host/32-gov-dns-realigned.png</code><span class="hint">Terminal capture (still at VBoS) of <code>resolvectl status eno8303</code> showing <code>DNS Servers: 10.255.134.24 10.255.134.5</code> and <code>DNS Domain: vangov.local</code>, plus a successful <code>dig</code> against a vangov.local name. Proves the DNS misconfiguration flagged in §6.1 is resolved.</span></div></div>
```

### Step C — Cutover (at NDMO, at power-up)

This is the only step that requires downtime. Executed **at the NDMO rack** after the
physical move and re-cabling. Use the iDRAC Virtual Console (now on its own NDMO static IP
via §14.5) to access the OS console — no crash cart required.

```bash
# 1. Activate the pre-staged static config and retire the VBoS-era file.
sudo mv /etc/netplan/99-ndmo-static.yaml.disabled \
        /etc/netplan/99-ndmo-static.yaml

sudo mv /etc/netplan/50-cloud-init.yaml \
        /root/50-cloud-init.yaml.vbos-era-$(date +%F)

# 2. Apply. Because netplan has only 98-gov-dns.yaml + 99-ndmo-static.yaml now,
#    the NDMO static block is authoritative.
sudo chmod 600 /etc/netplan/*.yaml
sudo netplan generate
sudo netplan try       # auto-reverts after 120 s unless you confirm
# If you can still reach the box from an NDMO seat on the new IP, press ENTER.
```

Update the hostname to match the NDMO-issued FQDN:

```bash
sudo hostnamectl set-hostname <NDMO-FQDN>       # e.g. ndmo-drmis-01.ndmo.gov.vu
```

Verify end-state:

```bash
ip -brief addr show eno8303        # Shows <NDMO-STATIC-IP>/<CIDR>, no 10.4.26.55
ip route                            # Default via <NDMO-GATEWAY>
resolvectl status eno8303           # DNS: 10.255.134.24, 10.255.134.5; search: vangov.local
hostname -f                         # <NDMO-FQDN>
curl -sSf -o /dev/null -w "local: %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1/
curl -sSf -o /dev/null -w "self : %{http_code}\n" http://<NDMO-STATIC-IP>/
```

```{=html}
<div class="screenshot-slot"><div class="screenshot-slot-inner"><strong>Figure 14.4.2 — Host on NDMO static IP (post-cutover)</strong><code>docs/screenshots/host/33-ndmo-static.png</code><span class="hint">Terminal capture at the NDMO rack: <code>ip -brief addr</code>, <code>ip route</code>, <code>hostname -f</code>, <code>resolvectl status eno8303</code>, and <code>curl</code> to <code>http://&lt;NDMO-STATIC-IP&gt;/</code>. This is the post-handover counterpart of Figure 6.1.1.</span></div></div>
```


### Step D — Application config realignment

Follow §14.6 to update `ALLOWED_HOSTS`, `DJANGO_VM_HOST`, nginx `server_name`, and the
frontend `VITE_API_HOST` to the new NDMO IP / FQDN, then restart the stack.

### §14.4.x — DHCP-detour fallback (use **only** if Step A is blocked)

If NDMO networking cannot pre-issue the static IP in time for Step A (e.g. change-control
lag), the server can be brought up on **DHCP** at the NDMO rack, given a temporary address,
and switched to static later. This costs an extra netplan cycle and is strictly worse than
Steps A–C above — use it only when Steps A–C are not feasible.

<details>
<summary>Expand for the DHCP-detour sequence</summary>

At the NDMO rack, via iDRAC Virtual Console:

```bash
sudo cp /etc/netplan/50-cloud-init.yaml \
        /root/50-cloud-init.yaml.pre-handover-$(date +%F)

echo 'network: {config: disabled}' | \
  sudo tee /etc/cloud/cloud.cfg.d/99-disable-network-config.cfg

sudo tee /etc/netplan/50-cloud-init.yaml >/dev/null <<'YAML'
# TEMPORARY — DHCP during NDMO handover cutover.
# Replace with final static block once NDMO-issued address arrives.
network:
  version: 2
  ethernets:
    eno8303:
      dhcp4: true
      dhcp6: false
YAML

sudo chmod 600 /etc/netplan/*.yaml
sudo netplan generate
sudo netplan apply
```

Record the DHCP-assigned IP (`ip -brief addr show eno8303`) — this is your SSH target until
Step C runs later with the real static values.

</details>

## 14.5 iDRAC network migration — preallocated-static cutover

iDRAC currently comes up on **DHCP** at `10.4.26.51`. It is already on the correct logical
network — domain `vangov.local`, DNS `10.255.134.24 / 10.255.134.5` — so only two things
change at handover:

1. Convert from DHCP to a **formally reserved NDMO-segment static IP**;
2. Enable **DNS auto-registration** so the iDRAC's `A` record is maintained in GoV DNS
   automatically when it lands on the new subnet.

As with the host OS (§14.4), the cleanest path is a **single-step cutover** — pre-set the
new static values via `racadm` while the iDRAC is still at VBoS, schedule them to take
effect at the next `racreset`, then let the first power-up at the NDMO rack bring the iDRAC
up directly on the new IP. No DHCP detour needed.

### Step A — Pre-stage the NDMO static on the iDRAC (at VBoS, before the move)

Values from NDMO networking:

- `<IDRAC-STATIC-IP>` and `<NETMASK>` (iDRAC management VLAN assignment)
- `<IDRAC-GATEWAY>`
- `<IDRAC-FQDN-SHORTNAME>` — short name only, e.g. `ndmo-drmis-01-idrac` (the full FQDN is
  `ndmo-drmis-01-idrac.vangov.local` once registered in GoV DNS)

Using the `racadm` wrapper from the host OS (§3.8):

```bash
# 1. Flip the IPv4 mode from DHCP to static and push the NDMO values in one transaction.
#    The new settings become effective at the next iDRAC reset.
racadm set iDRAC.IPv4.DHCPEnable 0
racadm set iDRAC.IPv4.Address    <IDRAC-STATIC-IP>
racadm set iDRAC.IPv4.Netmask    <NETMASK>
racadm set iDRAC.IPv4.Gateway    <IDRAC-GATEWAY>

# 2. DNS — already aligned with GoV, but make it explicit (no DHCP-supplied DNS).
racadm set iDRAC.IPv4.DNSFromDHCP  0
racadm set iDRAC.IPv4.DNS1         10.255.134.24
racadm set iDRAC.IPv4.DNS2         10.255.134.5

# 3. DNS registration — the iDRAC should register its own A record in GoV DNS.
racadm set iDRAC.NIC.DNSRacName        <IDRAC-FQDN-SHORTNAME>
racadm set iDRAC.NIC.DNSDomainName     vangov.local
racadm set iDRAC.NIC.DNSDomainFromDHCP 0
racadm set iDRAC.NIC.DNSRegister       1

# 4. NIC selection — already Dedicated on this host (the iDRAC has its own physical port).
racadm set iDRAC.NIC.Selection 1

# 5. Verify pending config before commit.
racadm get iDRAC.IPv4
racadm get iDRAC.NIC | grep -E 'DNS|Selection'
```

**Do not reset the iDRAC yet** — doing so at VBoS would immediately take the iDRAC off the
VBoS-segment network and you would lose remote access to it before the physical move. The
`racadm set` calls above stage the values; they take effect at the next `racreset` or at
the next power cycle, whichever comes first.

::: {.callout-important}
**Power-cycle timing matters.** If the server gets rebooted for any other reason between
Step A and the physical move (e.g. an unscheduled kernel update), the iDRAC *will* flip to
the NDMO static at that moment and disappear off the VBoS segment. If that happens before the
physical move, you must either:

- Postpone Step A until the day of the move, or
- Have NDMO pre-plumb the VBoS switch port to also reach the NDMO-segment IP (unusual), or
- Accept that the iDRAC is headless until the physical move completes.

Schedule Step A **on the day of the move**, after the last backup snapshot (§14.3) and
before shutdown.
:::

### Step B — Cutover (at NDMO, at first power-up)

1. Rack the server; cable the iDRAC dedicated NIC to the NDMO management VLAN port.
2. Power on.
3. During iDRAC POST initialisation (first 30–60 s), the iDRAC reads the staged config and
   brings up its dedicated NIC on `<IDRAC-STATIC-IP>`.
4. From an NDMO admin workstation, browse to `https://<IDRAC-STATIC-IP>/` and verify login
   as `root` (still the §14.7 password — rotation happens in §14.7.1, after sign-off).

Verify from the admin workstation:

```bash
ping -c3 <IDRAC-STATIC-IP>
curl -skI https://<IDRAC-STATIC-IP>/ | head -1       # HTTP/1.1 200 OK

# And the DNS registration (gives NDMO one less thing to forget):
dig +short <IDRAC-FQDN-SHORTNAME>.vangov.local       # Should return <IDRAC-STATIC-IP>
```

If the ping fails, Step A may not have taken effect (e.g. the power-off at VBoS was
graceful and fast enough that no `racreset` happened). Worst case, use the iDRAC Virtual
Console via a crash cart at the NDMO rack, re-run the `racadm set` block above on the host,
then `racadm racreset soft`.

### §14.5.x — DHCP-detour fallback (iDRAC)

If Step A cannot be pre-staged (e.g. the NDMO iDRAC IP reservation is not ready in time),
the iDRAC can be left on DHCP for the move and switched to static afterwards:

<details>
<summary>Expand for the iDRAC DHCP-detour sequence</summary>

At the NDMO rack, after the iDRAC NIC obtains an NDMO-DHCP lease, log into the iDRAC UI (or
use `racadm` from the host once the OS is up) and run the same `racadm set` block as Step A
above, followed by `racadm racreset soft`. The only difference from Step A is timing: the
reset happens at NDMO, not at VBoS.

</details>

## 14.6 Application configuration realignment

Once the host's IP has changed, three application-level settings must be updated so Django
accepts requests and the frontend can reach the API:

1. **`vbos-backend/.env`** — add the new host / FQDN to `ALLOWED_HOSTS` and (if used)
   `CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`. Keep old values if any external integrations still reference them.

2. **`deploy/vm/docker-compose.yml`** — update `DJANGO_VM_HOST`:

   ```yaml
   DJANGO_VM_HOST: http://<NDMO-STATIC-IP>   # or: https://<ndmo-fqdn> after TLS
   ```

3. **`vbos-frontend/.env.production.local`** — update the build-time API host:

   ```
   VITE_API_HOST=http://<NDMO-STATIC-IP>
   VITE_TITILER_API=http://<NDMO-STATIC-IP>:8002
   ```

Rebuild and restart:

```bash
cd /var/www/disaster-project-mis

# Rebuild frontend with new API host
cd vbos-frontend && pnpm install && pnpm build && cd ..

# Restart the stack to pick up new env vars
docker compose -f deploy/vm/docker-compose.yml up -d --force-recreate web nginx
```

Re-run the daily health check (§9.1) against the new IP and capture **Figure 9.1.1** again
with the new URLs.

## 14.7 Pre-handover credentials (CONFIDENTIAL)

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
**🔒 CONFIDENTIAL — handover package only.**

The credentials below are the **current, pre-handover** secrets held by **VBoS (the current
administrator)** while the server sits in the VBoS office, on the VBoS segment of the GoV network. They are recorded here
so they can be transferred to NDMO's password vault in one place during the physical handover
from VBoS. **They are not intended to live in this document long-term.**

### Handling policy — Option B (chosen)

Two handling policies were considered for this section:

- **Option A** — split the plaintext values into a separate `docs/.credentials.local.md` file
  and `.gitignore` that file, leaving only a pointer stub inside this `.qmd`.
- **Option B** — keep the plaintext values inline in this `.qmd` and instead ensure the file
   never reaches a non-internal git remote until §14.9 row 18 has rotated and sanitized it.

**Option B is in force.** The following guard-rails implement it:

1. **Public-remote finding.** As of the current commit, this repository's `origin` is
   `https://github.com/VBoS-Social-Section/disaster-project-mis` — a **public GitHub
   repository** (verified: `"private": false` via the GitHub API). That does **not** qualify
   as an internal remote. Therefore, until rotation, the file must not be pushed at all.
2. **`.gitignore` enforcement.** `docs/DMIS_HOST.qmd` is listed in `/var/www/disaster-project-mis/.gitignore`
   with a block comment pointing at this section. `git add docs/DMIS_HOST.qmd` is a no-op
   while that rule is in place, so the file cannot be pushed to *any* remote — public or
   private — by accident. Verify with:

    ```bash
    git check-ignore -v docs/DMIS_HOST.qmd
    # .gitignore:NN:docs/DMIS_HOST.qmd   docs/DMIS_HOST.qmd
    ```

3. **Distribution.** Transfer this document to the receiving NDMO sysadmin(s) **out-of-band**
   (encrypted USB, KeePass export, or a signed attachment over ministry email) — not via
   `git push`. The NDMO sysadmin loads the values into the NDMO password vault on arrival.
4. **Rotation deadline.** Within **24 hours of the NDMO sign-off in §14.9**, every value in
   this section must be rotated per §14.7.1 and **replaced with the marker
   `ROTATED <YYYY-MM-DD>, held in <vault-name>`** — no plaintext passwords retained.
5. **Commit the sanitized version.** §14.9 checklist row 18 is the single action that
   (a) confirms every plaintext value has been replaced with a `ROTATED` marker, (b) removes
   the `docs/DMIS_HOST.qmd` line from `.gitignore`, and (c) commits both changes in the same
   commit. Only then is the file allowed onto the public GitHub remote.
6. **Access control (pre-sign-off).** Access to this document is restricted to the VBoS
   sysadmin (pre-handover) and the designated NDMO sysadmins receiving handover. If the file
   is shared outside that set, treat every value as compromised and rotate immediately.

::: {.callout-warning}
If at any point during the handover the server's git remote is rehomed to an internal
ministry git server (e.g. a Gitea/GitLab instance on the NDMO network) **before** §14.9 step
14 runs, Option B still applies: the `.gitignore` rule stays in place until rotation, because
"internal" does not mean "safe to retain plaintext indefinitely" — row 4 of §14.9 still
requires the `ROTATED` markers within 24 hours.
:::
:::

## 14.7.1 Credential rotation (mandatory before sign-off)

::: {.callout-important}
Because **VBoS (the current administrator) has held every credential up to this point**,
every secret must be rotated at handover. No exceptions.
:::

| Credential | How | Where to store new value |
|---|---|---|
| `ndmoadmin` sudo password | `sudo passwd ndmoadmin` | NDMO password vault |
| `ndmoadmin` SSH authorized keys | Replace with NDMO admins' public keys; remove VBoS sysadmin's key | In-repo? No — in vault |
| iDRAC `root` account | Disable it entirely: `racadm set iDRAC.Users.2.Enable 0` | — |
| iDRAC named admin accounts | Delete any VBoS-era iDRAC accounts; create new per-NDMO-operator accounts (§3.4 step 6) | Vault |
| Django `SECRET_KEY` | Generate new: `python -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(64))'`; update `.env`; restart web | Vault |
| PostgreSQL `postgres` user | `ALTER USER postgres WITH PASSWORD '<new>'` inside the container + update `.env` + restart | Vault |
| Django superuser `admin` (`Double@1991`) | **Create per-operator NDMO superusers first** (§8.5.2), verify each can log into `/admin/`, then **deactivate** the shared `admin` account (§8.5.6 — preferred over deletion so existing foreign-key history is preserved) | Vault (record the new per-operator credentials; the retired `admin` needs no vault entry) |
| AWS / S3 keys (if any) | Rotate at the cloud provider; update `.env` | Vault |
| OpenAI API key (if set) | Rotate at OpenAI | Vault |
| TLS certificate (if issued in VBoS's name) | Re-issue in NDMO's name | — |

After rotation, **revoke VBoS's own access**:

- Remove the VBoS sysadmin's SSH public key from `~ndmoadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys`;
- Delete their iDRAC account (or disable it);
- Confirm they can no longer SSH in or log into iDRAC.

## 14.8 Smoke tests (NDMO-side)

Performed by an NDMO operator, **not** a VBoS operator, using only the new credentials and
the new NDMO-network IP:

1. SSH in: `ssh ndmoadmin@<NDMO-IP>` — should succeed.
2. `sudo -l` — should work with the new sudo password.
3. Log into iDRAC UI at the new IP with a new NDMO admin account — should succeed.
4. Attempt to log into iDRAC with the old `root` / `calvin` — **must fail** (account disabled).
5. Browser: open DRMIS at `http://<NDMO-IP>/` — SPA renders.
6. Browser: log into Django admin at `http://<NDMO-IP>/admin/` with the newly created NDMO
   superuser — succeeds.
7. On the map: at least one base layer + one vector layer + one raster layer renders (proves
   nginx → web / titiler / PMTiles paths all work).
8. Run §9.1 health-check script — all endpoints return 200/302.
9. From a workstation **outside** NDMO LAN: confirm neither the server nor iDRAC are reachable
   (proving perimeter firewall is correctly scoped).

and captures, and commit the updates:

```bash
cd /var/www/disaster-project-mis

# 1. Sanitize §14.7 — replace every plaintext password with a ROTATED marker.
#    e.g.  Password | ROTATED 2026-05-01, held in NDMO-KeePass/DRMIS

# 2. Remove the DMIS_HOST.qmd block from .gitignore (the Option B safety net).
sed -i '/^docs\/DMIS_HOST\.qmd$/d;/^docs\/\.credentials\.local\.md$/d' .gitignore
# Also delete the surrounding TEMPORARY comment block in .gitignore by hand.

# 3. Fill in the remaining TO-BE-VERIFIED fields and swap screenshot slots
#    for ![caption](screenshots/host/NN-name.png) markdown.

# 4. Commit the sanitized doc AND the .gitignore cleanup in the same commit
#    (this is §14.9 checklist row 18).
git add .gitignore docs/DMIS_HOST.qmd docs/screenshots/host/
git commit -m "docs(host): post-handover sanitize — rotated markers + screenshots"
git push
```

::: {.callout-important}
Until step 2 above runs, `git add docs/DMIS_HOST.qmd` is a silent no-op (the file is ignored
by the Option B guard in `.gitignore`). That is **intentional** — it is what prevents the
plaintext credentials in §14.7 from ever reaching the public GitHub remote.
:::

# Appendix A — Command cheat sheet

## Identity & health

```bash
hostnamectl
uname -a
uptime
free -h
df -h
lscpu
timedatectl
```

## Hardware

```bash
# From sysfs (no root needed)
cat /sys/class/dmi/id/{sys_vendor,product_name,product_sku,bios_version,bios_date}

# With root
sudo dmidecode -t system
sudo dmidecode -t memory
sudo dmidecode -t bios
sudo dmidecode -t 39           # Power supplies
sudo ipmitool sensor
sudo ipmitool fru
sudo ipmitool sel list
```

## iDRAC (once racadm is installed — §3.8)

```bash
racadm getsysinfo              # Summary
racadm getversion              # Firmware versions
racadm get iDRAC.IPv4          # iDRAC IP
racadm gethwinventory
racadm storage get controllers
racadm storage get vdisks
racadm storage get pdisks
racadm getsel
racadm serveraction powercycle # Dangerous — forces reset
```

## Networking

```bash
ip -brief addr
ip route
ss -tlnp
resolvectl status
sudo ufw status verbose
```

## Docker / application

```bash
cd /var/www/disaster-project-mis
docker compose -f deploy/vm/docker-compose.yml ps
docker compose -f deploy/vm/docker-compose.yml logs -f --tail=200 web
docker compose -f deploy/vm/docker-compose.yml exec web ./manage.py migrate
docker compose -f deploy/vm/docker-compose.yml exec postgres psql -U postgres -d vbos
docker system df
```

```bash
fwupdmgr get-devices
sudo fwupdmgr refresh
sudo fwupdmgr update
```
